verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो द्रोणे हते राजन् दुर्योधनमुखा नृपाः । भृशमुद्विग्नमनसो द्रोणपुत्रमुपागमन् ॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said O king, after Drona had been killed, the monarchs headed by Duryodhana, with greatly anxious hearts, all went to the son of Drona.

verses.sanskrit: ते द्रोणमनुशोचन्तः कश्मलाभिहतौजसः । पर्युपासन्त शोकार्तास्ततः शारद्वतीसुतम् ॥२॥
verses.english: Thereupon mourning for the death of Drona, they (the kings) being highly oppressed with grief and deprived of energy on account of their gloominess of mind sat around the son of Sharadvata.
verses.bhavadeepa: ननु विराटादिपर्वचतुष्टयतात्पर्यं क्रमेणार्थलुब्धानामर्थः सेवया नीत्या कपटपूर्वकेण कुलवृद्धवधेन नृशंसानृतपूर्वकेण महागुरुवधेन च सिद्ध्यतीत्युक्तम् । तावतैवार्थनिरूपणं समाप्तम् अतः परं काममोक्षावेव निरूपणीयाविति कर्णपर्वादित्रयं नारम्भणीयमिति चेत् सत्यम् । यथा धर्मार्थौ निरूपितौ एवं धर्माभासोऽर्थाभासश्च निरूपणीयः परिहाराय । एवमधर्मानर्थौ अधर्माभासानर्थाभासौ च निरूपणीयौ हानायोपादानाय च तदर्थमुत्तरग्रन्थः काममोक्षयोः प्रागावश्यकः । तत्र चोरेभ्यः कार्पटिकमार्गमुपदिशतः सत्यवादिनः सत्यवदनं धर्माभासः। एवमविचार्य घ्राणचक्षुषं राक्षसं घ्नतो व्याधस्य हिंस्रत्वमधर्माभासः । तथा शोकहेतुना कुलक्षयेण प्राप्तोऽर्थोऽर्थाभासः । सुप्तानां हननमधर्मः । तत्कृतोऽश्वत्थाम्नोऽभिभवोऽनर्थः। शरणागतस्वसैनिकत्राणार्थमन्यायेनापि कृतो ब्रह्मवधो न इतरब्रह्मवधवदनर्थः । अपि त्वनर्थाभास एव । न च तेन ब्रह्महा भवेदित्याततायिवधे दोषाभावस्मरणात् । इत्येषामर्थानां निरूपणार्थ उत्तरः संदर्भः । आख्यायिका तु सुखप्रतिपत्त्यर्था । तस्मादिदमपि पर्वत्रयमावश्यकमेव । ततो द्रोणे हते राजन्निति ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: ते मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य हेतुभिः शास्त्रसम्मितैः । रात्र्यागमे महीपालाः स्वानि वेश्मानि भेजिरे ॥३॥
verses.english: Then having comforted him for a short while by citing reasons arrived at in the Shastras, the rulers of the earth departed to their respective abodes on the advent of the night.

verses.sanskrit: ते वेश्मस्वपि कौरव्य पृथ्वीशा नामुवन्सुखम् । चिन्तयन्तः क्षयं तीव्रं दुःखशोकसमन्विताः ॥४॥
verses.english: O descendant of the Kuru race, the lords of the earth could not enjoy pleasure while resting in their own abodes; and they could not obtain sleep, thinking of that immense massacre.

verses.sanskrit: विशेषतः सूतपुत्रो राजा चैव सुयोधनः । दुःशासनश्च शकुनिः सौबलश्च महाबलः ॥५॥
verses.english: Especially the son of Suta, king Suyodhana, Dushasana and Shakuni could not at all sleep.
verses.bhavadeepa: पृथ्वीशाः राजानः क्षयं भूतं भाविनं च चिन्तयन्तः परामृशन्तः ॥४॥

verses.sanskrit: उषितास्ते निशां तां तु दुर्योधननिवेशने । चिन्तयन्तः परिक्लेशान् पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम् ॥६॥
verses.english: And they passed together that night in the abode of Duryodhana, whilst they were seriously thinking of the grief's with which the lofty-minded Pandavas were afflicted.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तद्यूते परिक्लिष्टा कृष्णा चानायिता सभाम् । तत्स्मरन्तोऽनुशोचन्तो भृशमुद्विग्नचेतसः ॥७॥
verses.english: Recollecting these, viz. that they (the Pandavas) were greatly oppressed during the game at dice and also that Krishna (Draupadi) was (forcibly) brought to the assembly (of kings), they greatly regretted, with hearts filled with anxiety.

verses.sanskrit: तथा तु संचिन्तयतां तान् क्लेशान् द्यूतकारितान् । दुःखेन क्षणदा राजन् जगामाब्दशतोपमा ॥८॥
verses.english: Thus reflecting upon those miseries resulting from the gambling match, (which the Pandavas had become subject to), their night had passed away with great uneasiness, which (night), O king, seemed to be (so long as) a hundred years.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रभाते विमले स्थिता दिष्टस्य शासने । चक्रुरावश्यकं सर्वे विधिदिष्टेन कर्मणा ॥९॥
verses.english: Thereupon at the break of day they, being obedient to the injunctions of ordinance, all performed the necessary ceremonies, prescribed by the established usage.

verses.sanskrit: ते कृत्वाऽवश्यकार्याणि समाश्वस्य च भारत । योगमाज्ञापयामासुर्युद्धाय च विनिर्ययुः ॥१०॥
verses.english: Having finished all the necessary ceremonies and consoled themselves, they, O Bharata, ordered for the array of soldiers and then started for battle.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णं सेनापतिं कृत्वा कृतकौतुकमङ्गलाः । पूजयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठान् दधिपात्रघृताक्षतैः ॥११॥
verses.english: After having made Karna their generalissimo with the due performance of the most auspicious rites (by tying a thread round his wrist) and having adored the foremost of the regenerate persons by offerings of vessels of curds, clarified butter and vessels, filled with corn and other auspicious articles, as well as by presents of gold-coins, kine and gems, valuable cloths and immense wealth and also having been praised by the charioteers and panegyrists, born in the country of Magadha, (the Magadha-panegyrists are the mixed tribes born of a Kshatriya mother and a Brahmana father), with hymns about victory.

verses.sanskrit: गोभिरश्वैश्च निष्कैश्च वासोभिश्च महाधनैः। वन्द्यमाना जयाशीर्भिः सूत-मागध-बन्दिभिः ॥१२॥
तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् कृतपूर्वाह्निकक्रियाः । शिबिरान्निर्ययुस्तूर्णं युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयाः ॥१३॥
verses.english: O monarch, the Pandavas on the other hand, having similarly performed the morning ceremonies, came out of their tents; and O king, they were resolved upon the battle.
verses.bhavadeepa: निष्कैः सुवर्णहारैः महाधनैः बहुमूल्यैः वन्द्यमानाः स्तूयमानाः सूताः वंशानुक्रमविदः मागधाः पाणिस्वनिकाः वन्दिनः स्तुतिपाठकाः ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम् । कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च परस्परजयैषिणाम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: Thereupon the formidable battle began, which caused the hair of the body stand erect, between the Kurus and the Pandavas, each party being desirous of vanquishing the other.

verses.sanskrit: तयोर्द्वौ दिवसौ युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः । कर्णे सेनापतौ राजन् बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: O monarch, the most formidable battle, betwcen the troops of the Kurus and those of the Pandavas, lasted only for two days during the leadership of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शत्रुक्षयं कृत्वा सुमहान्तं रणे वृषः । पश्यतां धार्तराष्ट्राणां फाल्गुनेन निपातितः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Thereupon Vrisha (Karna), having brought about an immense slaughter of the opponents in battle, was himself slain by Falguna (Arjuna), whilst the sons of Dhartarashtra were observing it.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु सञ्जयः सर्वं गत्वा नागपुरं द्रुतम् । आचष्ट धृतराष्ट्राय यद्वृत्तं कुरुजाङ्गले ॥१७॥
verses.english: Thereafter Sanjaya departed towards the city of Hastinapur and told all to Dhritarashtra, that had taken place at Kurujangala.

verses.sanskrit:
जनमेजय उवाच।
              आपगेयं हतं श्रुत्वा द्रोणं चापि महारथम् । आजगाम परामार्तिं वृद्धो राजाऽम्बिकासुतः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Janamejaya said Having heard that both Bhishma and the car-warrior Drona of indomitable courage were slain (in the battle), the old king (Dhritarashtra) the son of Ambika, was highly oppressed with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: स श्रुत्वा निहतं कर्णं दुर्योधनहितैषिणम् । कथं द्विजवर प्राणानधारयत दुःखितः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Having heard of the death of Karna the benefactor of Duryodhana, how could he, O best of the regenerate persons, hold his life, much aggrieved as he was?

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिञ्जयाशां पुत्राणां सममन्यत पार्थिवः । तस्मिन् हते स कौरव्यः कथं प्राणानधारयत्॥२०॥
verses.english: How could that royal descendant of Kuru hold his life, after having heard of the fall of that hero, on whom he supposed the hope of his sons' victory to rest?

verses.sanskrit: दुर्मरं तदहं मन्ये नृणां कृछ्रेऽपि वर्तताम् । यत्र कर्णं हतं श्रुत्वा नात्यजज्जीवितं नृपः ॥२१॥
verses.english: I suppose that men, falling in the most distressful circumstances, find greatest difficulty in yielding up their lives; for, the king, even after hearing of the death of Karna, could not (possibly) forsake his life.

verses.sanskrit: तथा शान्तनवं वृद्धं ब्रह्मन् बाह्लीकमेव च । द्रोणं च सोमदत्तं च भूरिश्रवसमेव च ॥२२॥
verses.english: As, O twice-born one, having heard of the fall of the old son of Shantanu, of Balhika, of Drona, of Somadatta, of Bhurisravas, as well as of other friends, of his sons and grandsons, the king did not give up his life; so, I suppose, that to yield up one's life is, O regenerate person, highly difficult.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव चान्यान्सुहृदः पुत्रान् पौत्रांश्च पातितान् । श्रुत्वा यन्नाजहात्प्राणांस्तन्मन्ये दुष्करं द्विज ॥२३॥
एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व विस्तरेण महामुने । न हि तृप्यामि पूर्वेषां शृण्वानश्चरितं महत्॥२४॥
verses.english: Relate to me all these in their entirety, as they had really taken place. I am not (at all) satisfied with (simply) hearing the mighty achievements of my forefathers.
